quotes.text: Are you… 1 single, that is never married 2 married and living with your husband/wife 3 a civil partner in a legally-recognised Civil Partnership 4 married and separated from your husband/wife 5 Divorced 6 or widowed
Is [Name’s] husband/wife/civil partner a member of the household? 1 Yes 2 No
I would now like to ask how all the people in your household are related to each other. Code relationship of [Name] to [Name]
You told me that [NumHhldrs] people jointly own or rent the accommodation. Which of you/them has the highest income (from earnings, benefits, pensions and any other sources)?

assessments.reasoning: The survey allows distinguishing de jure vs de facto headship status because it collects marital status in XMARSTA alongside explicit partner presence/absence in MARCHK and LIV12W. It allows identifying unpartnered mother-child units across the household through the person-to-person relationship matrix R combined with cohabitation and marital status variables. However, it does not identify women-maintained households/units through the main provider regardless of reference person, as HIHNUM only asks for the person with highest income among joint owners/renters rather than across all household members. Lastly, the questionnaire contains no module or mechanism to link mother-child units/hearth-holds to their own consumption, production, or care activity.
